name: MA-04
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's strong Democratic lean of about 11 points on the partisan voting index
Incumbent Jake Auchincloss holds a massive financial advantage, with $7.3 million on hand versus roughly $1,300 for his Republican opponent
Prediction markets price the Democratic side at about 97 percent to win
No competitive outside spending or notable general-election polling against the incumbent
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly Democratic: an 11-point partisan lean, a two-term incumbent, and a favorable national environment, with Auchincloss out-raising Thomas Stalcup by more than a hundred to one. Markets and the absence of any expert-rated competition both corroborate a safe Democratic seat, so the forecast stays at the fundamentals-implied margin.
model.watch: Any late surge of outside spending against Auchincloss or an unexpectedly strong Republican fundraising quarter would be the first sign this race deserves a second look.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Massachusetts' 4th District leans about 11 points Democratic, and second-term incumbent Jake Auchincloss is running for reelection with a commanding financial position. He has raised over $3.6 million and holds $7.3 million in cash, while Republican Thomas Stalcup has raised roughly $26,000 and reported just over $1,000 on hand. No outside groups are spending against the incumbent.

No expert raters list this race as competitive, and no general-election polling is available, so the outlook rests on fundamentals. Prediction markets price the Democratic side at about 97 percent, consistent with a comfortable double-digit expected margin. The race is rated Safe Democratic.
